name: Dike route
text: [approach] Snow on the dike and the face can be scouted from there before committing.
[descent_text] Many parties do not go on to the summit at all: after the Dike Pinnacle they bail out by dropping into Garnet Canyon's south fork, or by heading north onto the Middle Teton Glacier.
[descent_text] The ground from the pinnacle to Ellingwood Col is convoluted and needs a rappel, and the col itself is a steep snow crossing of about 40 degrees that holds snow all year.
earlierWhy: Ellingwood Col is a steep snow crossing that holds snow all year.

name: East Face
text: [overview] Gain the bottom of it by continuing up the gully below the glacier and turning right.
earlierWhy: A glacier is mentioned only as a landmark.

name: West Face
text: [overview] P1: the lone significant break in the lower headwall leads, via a chimney of great cracks, to an overhang (snow and ice early in the year), then a crumbly low-angle slab to a slung block (5.6, 35m).
[approach] early in the season it is a tongue of snow and ice over a short overhang, later a chimney.
[descent_text] Then rappel to the snow or choss gully, downclimb it, and rappel to the base.
earlierWhy: Snow and ice noted for early in the year only.

name: Lookin for Trouble
text: [detailed_rack] universal crampons and an axe, depending on the conditions.

name: Big Jobbin
text: [approach] It begins by ascending a snowfield to clean cracks in the middle right of the buttress.
[descent_text] The alternative is a series of double-rope rappels from the top of the fifth pitch down to the bottom of the snowfield.

name: North Side Lowlight Tour (path of least resistance)
text: [overview] 6-7: ledge, 4th/easy 5th, then easy snow/3rd.

[approach] The climb starts at the top of the Grandstand, reached as for the North Face Highlight Tour: the Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle, up the Grandstand from the Teton Glacier, or from Mt.
[approach] The Valhalla Traverse is the standard and starts at the Lower Saddle, while the Teton Glacier approach tends to see rockfall.
earlierWhy: Standard approach is the Valhalla Traverse; glacier approach optional.

name: Northeast Couloir
text: [watch_out] only climb in ideal snow conditions with confirmed low/minimal avalanche hazard.
[watch_out] Entry and exit of steep couloir can be technical with snow or ice up to 60 degrees—difficult down-climbing if route-finding error occurs;
[watch_out] requires excellent snow/ice judgment.
[watch_out] Bergschrund crossing at glacier base—may be significant obstacle early/mid-season with potential fall hazard;
[watch_out] Late-season glacier becomes bare ice (July+)—surface becomes extremely difficult and icy;
[watch_out] crampons and ice tools essential;
[watch_out] Crevasses in upper Colchuck Glacier approach (though fewer than on other glacier routes)—travel roped;
earlierWhy: Text describes a different range (Colchuck); snow couloir though.

name: South West Couloir
text: [overview] Classic unroped climbing tops the route, shared with the Triple Glaciers route (northwest face).
[detailed_rack] Crampons and an ice tool, a rope that is short and thin, and thin pieces (a few).
[approach] Early in the season the snow is flat and white before mid May.
[descent_text] Crampons and an ice tool are standard in snowy conditions.
earlierWhy: Crampons standard in snowy conditions only.

name: Stettner Couloir
text: [overview] A steep couloir between two ridges on the south side of the Grand Teton, giving a snow and ice route to the summit in early summer.
[overview] As the season advances the snow melts out and rock climbing appears in the upper couloir, ending with a short rock step onto the broad southeast face.
[hazards] Exposed to avalanches spilling from the adjacent Ford Couloir, which catches early sun and fresh snow in late spring.
[hazards] Difficulty is highly condition-dependent — can be a moderate WI2-3 snow climb one season and a 5.7 waterfall-ice rock climb another
[gear] Crampons are a must;
[gear] Two 60 m ropes are ideal, both for a full-length rappel retreat and for the common ski/glacier descent.
[gear] Gear needs shift by season — expect more snow/ice tools in spring/early summer, more rock rack in late summer and fall
[detailed_rack] On snow and ice: small cams (a couple) or screws (a couple).
[approach] or come from the east via the Teepe Glacier, Teepe Col and Glencoe Col, which is the more common approach.
[descent_text] Above the chockstone crux the couloir broadens to the narrow saddle between the Underhill Ridge and the summit snowfield.
[descent_text] Turn left, climb third-class slabs mixed with snow, and take the best line up the snowfield to the top.
earlierWhy: Snow and ice route in early summer; common approach crosses the Teepe Glacier.

name: Glencoe-Teepe Chute
text: [approach] A long snow slope leads to the base of the gully.
[approach] Steep snow slopes here are avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
[descent_text] From the col, the way down is the Teepe Glacier.
earlierWhy: Winter gully with snow slope; descent is the Teepe Glacier.

name: The Grand Traverse
text: [hazards] Snow and ice coverage varies year to year and changes the difficulty significantly.
[gear] Ice axe and crampons, needed or not depending on the season's snow coverage.
earlierWhy: Snow coverage varies year to year.

name: Underhill Ridge Original/Direct
text: [hazards] Upper mountain may require snow travel depending on time of year.
[gear] Ice axe and crampons if snow lingers on the upper slopes.
[approach] The alternative is to camp at the foot of the Teepe Glacier and climb up from there, which usually needs an ice axe and sometimes crampons for an early start.
[approach] Glencoe Col can also be bivied, with snow for water.
[descent_text] snow higher up may call for detours.
earlierWhy: Snow depends on time of year.

name: Ice of Desperation
text: [overview] Steep snow leads up into the couloir, where a 20 m smear of ice waits.
[overview] Pitch 2 is a snow slog for the remainder of the couloir.
[approach] The line is the central, northeast-facing couloir: follow the highest snow to its top at the base of the buttress.
[approach] Protection is scarce on the snow above the ice, so check the avalanche forecast.
earlierWhy: Winter couloir ice and snow climb; glacier not stated.

name: Wind Walker Traverse
text: [detailed_rack] an ice axe and crampons are needed on Gannett.
earlierWhy: Axe and crampons needed on Gannett.
